ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a square with both diagonals drawn. A gray shaded quadrilateral lies on the right side of the square. The extra slanted segment is parallel to the bottom-left-to-top-right diagonal and connects the midpoint of the bottom side to the midpoint of the right side, as indicated by matching tick marks. Reasoning: Let the square be the unit square with vertices (0,0), (1,0), (1,1), and (0,1). The two diagonals are y=x and y=1-x. The extra slanted segment from the bottom midpoint (1/2,0) to the right midpoint (1,1/2) has equation y=x-1/2. It intersects y=1-x at x-1/2=1-x, so 2x=3/2 and x=3/4, giving the point (3/4,1/4). Thus the shaded quadrilateral has vertices (1/2,1/2), (1,1), (1,1/2), and (3/4,1/4). Using the shoelace formula, its area is 1/2 |(1/2)(1)+1(1/2)+1(1/4)+(3/4)(1/2) - ((1/2)(1)+1(1)+(1/2)(3/4)+(1/4)(1/2))| = 1/2 |13/8 - 2| = 3/16. Since the square has area 1, the shaded fraction is 3/16.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates. Read the diagram as a unit square with both diagonals drawn, and with the extra slanted segment joining the midpoint of the bottom side to the midpoint of the right side, as indicated by the matching tick marks. Let the square have vertices (0,0), (1,0), (1,1), (0,1). The diagonals are y=x and y=1-x. The midpoint connector has equation y=x-1/2, meeting the right side at (1,1/2) and meeting the diagonal y=1-x at (3/4,1/4). The shaded region is the quadrilateral with vertices (1/2,1/2), (1,1), (1,1/2), and (3/4,1/4). Compute its area by the shoelace formula, or split it into coordinate triangles, and divide by the unit square area to get 3/16.

method.method_draft: Use triangle similarity inside the right-side triangle formed by the two diagonals. From the image, the two diagonals divide the square into four congruent triangles, so the right triangle with vertices at the top-right corner, bottom-right corner, and the diagonal intersection has area 1/4 of the square. The shaded region is this right-side triangle with a smaller bottom-right triangle removed. The tick marks show the extra slanted line passes through the midpoint of the right side, and it is parallel to the diagonal from the center to the top-right corner. Therefore, by the midpoint theorem, it cuts the other side of the right-side triangle at its midpoint, making the small removed triangle similar to the whole right-side triangle with scale factor 1/2. Its area is therefore 1/4 of 1/4, or 1/16 of the square. Subtract: 1/4 - 1/16 = 3/16.
